findings.highlight: The boy, who said he’d protect the girl
findings.evidenceJa: “守る”と繰り返した少年
findings.governingReading: The boy repeatedly tells himself that he will protect Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English turns the repeated promise into a single statement.

findings.evidenceJa: 残された薄闇
findings.governingReading: Sakura remains in the room’s thin, dim gloom.
findings.explanation: The English intensifies the subdued half-darkness into full darkness.

findings.evidenceJa: 苦しげに吐息を漏らす
findings.governingReading: Sakura lets out a pained breath.
findings.explanation: The English changes restrained breath into a vocal moan.

findings.highlight: The boy threw away his self
findings.evidenceJa: 少年は自分を捨てて
findings.governingReading: Shirou abandons himself or his own interests in choosing to believe Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and obscures the self-abandonment central to Sakura’s guilt.

findings.highlight: she will not be able to see him again
findings.evidenceJa: まっすぐにあの人と向き合えなくなる
findings.governingReading: Sakura fears she could no longer face Shirou honestly and directly if she became like the dream.
findings.explanation: The English changes a moral inability to face him into never encountering him again.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼の心を壊してしまった
findings.governingReading: Sakura believes she has irreparably broken Shirou’s heart.
findings.explanation: The English changes emotional injury into destruction of his mind.

findings.highlight: A person exists that will protect her
findings.evidenceJa: こんな自分でも、守ると言ってくれたモノがある
findings.governingReading: Even within this degraded self, something remains that Shirou said he would protect.
findings.explanation: The English turns the protected remnant of Sakura into the existence of a person who protects her.

findings.evidenceJa: そのカタチがまだ少しでも残っているのなら
findings.governingReading: If even a little of the self or form Shirou promised to protect remains, Sakura must restrain herself.
findings.explanation: The English removes the fragile residual form and reduces it to Sakura still remaining.

findings.highlight: There’s something that cannot be returned
findings.evidenceJa: もう、戻らないものがある
findings.governingReading: Something has been lost that will no longer return.
findings.explanation: The English uses a transitive “returned,” making the loss awkward and unclear.

findings.highlight: a crime that she cannot atone for with the life that remains to her
findings.evidenceJa: この先、どんなに生きても償えない罪
findings.governingReading: Sakura believes the crime cannot be atoned for however long she may live from this point onward.
findings.explanation: The English replaces unlimited duration with the finite remainder of her present life.

findings.evidenceJa: 半刻前
findings.governingReading: The recollection begins half a koku earlier, approximately one hour.
findings.explanation: The English halves the elapsed time.

findings.highlight: She knows that he came to kill her
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を殺す為にやってきた事は空気でわかる
findings.governingReading: Sakura believes she can sense from the atmosphere that Shirou came intending to kill her.
findings.explanation: The English promotes her perception of intent into unqualified knowledge.

findings.evidenceJa: その殺意は空っぽだった
findings.governingReading: The killing intent Sakura senses is empty.
findings.explanation: The English weakens specific intent to kill into general hostility.

findings.evidenceJa: 冷たい風が通り過ぎている
findings.governingReading: Cold wind whistles and passes through the hole Sakura imagines in Shirou’s chest.
findings.explanation: The English uses “blazing” for cold wind, breaking the physical image.

findings.evidenceJa: どんなに頑張っても体の震えは止まらなかった
findings.governingReading: No matter how hard Sakura tried, she could not stop her body trembling.
findings.explanation: The English states the result but omits her sustained effort against it.

findings.highlight: he will accept the crime she committed and will commit
findings.evidenceJa: 全部一緒になって受ける
findings.governingReading: Sakura reads Shirou’s arms as promising to share and bear together all her past and future guilt.
findings.explanation: The English retains acceptance but omits bearing it together with her.

findings.evidenceJa: 夕焼けの校庭
findings.governingReading: The remembered setting is the schoolyard at sunset.
findings.explanation: The English changes the concrete schoolyard into the school as a whole.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠い少年
findings.governingReading: The boy in Sakura’s memory is distant from her.
findings.explanation: The English removes the distance defining her original act of watching.

findings.evidenceJa: ずっと、その望みを叶えてきた
findings.governingReading: Through continuing visits to the Emiya house, Sakura has gone on fulfilling that wish all this time.
findings.explanation: The English collapses a sustained life pattern into one completed fulfillment.

findings.highlight: I swore to be your superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の味方をするって誓った
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls swearing to stand on Sakura’s side.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the morally central ally vow with an unsupported superhero claim.

findings.highlight: She wanted to protect the boy
findings.evidenceJa: 大切な人を守りたかった
findings.governingReading: Sakura wanted to protect Shirou as her precious person.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the protective wish but omits the relational value she assigns him.

findings.highlight: The girl makes her final resolution
findings.evidenceJa: 気を引き締めていなければ途切れていく時間の中
findings.governingReading: Sakura makes her decision in time that threatens to cut out unless she keeps herself braced and attentive.
findings.explanation: The English removes her failing continuity of consciousness and the effort required to remain present.

findings.highlight: Had he tried to take your life
findings.evidenceJa: 彼がサクラに手をあげていれば
findings.governingReading: Rider says she would have killed Shirou had he raised a hand against or attacked Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English narrows Rider’s trigger from an attack to an attempt on Sakura’s life.

findings.evidenceJa: 私はマトウサクラを守るだけ
findings.governingReading: Rider insists that whatever Sakura becomes, she protects the person designated “Matou Sakura.”
findings.explanation: The English replaces the identity-bearing proper name with “you,” weakening the paradox Sakura immediately tests.

findings.evidenceJa: それは口にしてはならない事
findings.governingReading: Rider gives no answer because the implication is something that must not be spoken aloud.
findings.explanation: The English’s pronoun most naturally assigns the prohibition to Sakura, obscuring Rider’s silence.

findings.evidenceJa: 強く拳を握る
findings.governingReading: Sakura strongly clenches one fist.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the gesture.

findings.highlight: raises her hand in the darkness
findings.evidenceJa: 左手を闇に掲げる
findings.governingReading: Sakura raises her left hand, the hand bearing her final Command Spell.
findings.explanation: The English omits the side needed to bind the gesture to the spell.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔術行使
findings.governingReading: Rider warns Sakura against performing magecraft in her bodily condition.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the setting’s technical practice with generic magic.

findings.highlight: They are weak, but they are eyes of determination that belong to a magus
findings.evidenceJa: 弱々しくも、決意を固めた魔術師の瞳
findings.governingReading: Though Sakura is physically weak, her gaze is that of a magus whose resolve is firm.
findings.explanation: The English assigns weakness to the eyes and renders the resolved-magus image in awkward possessive prose.
